newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans fall further, meal down sharply.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans fall further, meal down sharply.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures were down more than half the 30-cent per bushel daily limit as Cargill Inc sold at least five million bushels, traders said.
Soymeal was also sharply lower on commercial and fund selling.

Traders said the market shrugged off news USDA cut soybean ending stocks to 125 million bushels in Friday's Supply and Demand Report and focused instead on indications recent price gains were rationing demand.
They pointed to the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush figure of 25.94 million bushels.
That figure was below trade expectations and the lowest since the October 10 weekly report.
Traders said Cargill sold 300 lots July soymeal and 100 December while Refco Inc sold at least 400 lots July and 100 May.
At 1104 CDT, soybeans were down 17-1/2 to one cent per bushel with May down 17-1/4 at $8.39-1/2 a bushel. Soymeal was down $7.00 to $0.80 per ton with May down $7.00 at $277.00.
